scope: All 51 whole-token sovršen-/nesovršen-/nesoveršen- forms in the live v019 Latin corpus. Every site denotes the field-theoretic terms perfect field or imperfect field; none denotes grammatical aspect, completed action, or ordinary personal perfection.
choice: Use the official type-1 hard-adjective family doskonaly for perfect fields and nedoskonaly for imperfect fields, inflected exactly for gender, number, and case. The defining paragraph at base-papers1-43-isv.tex line 15339 remains the reader-facing semantic anchor.
motivation: The inherited sovršen- family is an official type-2 RU/SH-derived choice with an explicitly Polish-negative profile. The official type-1 doskonaly entry connects the independent West-Slavic dokonal-/doskonał- family with Belarusian and Ukrainian cognates, while the mathematical definition makes the term recoverable for South-Slavic readers whose native sources use savršen- or the international perfekt- family. This changes the dominant-language morphology without changing Noether's field-theoretic distinction.
alternatives_rejected: Retain sovršen-/nesovršen- and fix only nesoveršeno: this preserves the exact East/South-heavy type-2 collapse the normalization is intended to remove.

Introduce unattested official-lexicon adjective perfektny: Czech and Slovene mathematical sources support the international technical family, but the current official Interslavic lexicon contains no such adjective and perfekt also names a grammatical tense; it remains comparator evidence rather than the house lemma.
Use dokončeny or popolny: these mean completed or full/complete and would blur the algebraic definition of a perfect field.
Print a doublet at every occurrence: the definition already supplies the meaning, while repeated doublets would damage readable mathematical prose and terminology consistency.
Select by raw source-token volume: the Czech, Slovene, Bosnian, Polish, Belarusian, and Ukrainian evidence represents independent language families and is not a token vote.

german_meaning_authority.finding: The aligned source consistently uses the technical pair vollkommener/unvollkommener Körper, including the explicit definition, theorem headings, coefficient fields, and splitting fields.
